paper_title: A Spectral Approach to Approximately Counting Independent Sets in Dense Bipartite Graphs
classifications: Theory of computation → Approximation algorithms analysis
Theory of computation → Algorithm design techniques
statement: 1. Naturally, a next goal is to understand the power and limitations of the methods presented, especially in conjunction with existing cluster expansion methods. More specifically, we are curious about the following two questions: a. Can this spectral point of view help with our understanding of independent sets in a larger class of bipartite graphs? b. To what extent do these methods help in reducing the computation needed to implement algorithmic cluster expansion? In this context, the problem of approximating the number of independent sets in small-set expanders feels within striking distance. 2. Our next remark concerns Lemma 9. As mentioned before, similar results have had other applications in optimization and Unique Games [2, 36, 37], though we take a subtly different viewpoint worth noting: we seek to approximate all cuts in the graph, not just small ones. In any case, we find the lemma interesting in its own right and conjecture something stronger.
